withdrawnVersions.reason: The plugin claimed Gateway's unique shared /api RPC interceptor and broke Desktop welcome API requests. The old packed RPC-only checks did not cover Gateway coexistence.

notes: This record consumes the successful frozen pre-final packed test on DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 (cordis 4.1.0). After documentation/compatibility metadata changes, the exact final tarball must be repacked, installed and checked separately. Its complete payload and SHA256 remain in external final-artifact evidence to avoid a self-referential hash.

The real Gateway settings/describe and Desktop welcome llm/listConfigurableProviders requests succeeded with the plugin installed, after a real owned Host restart while still installed, and after uninstall. Remote payloads use {args:{}}; Settings namespaces and provider directories may be empty, and no plugin live-form namespace is required.

Plugin RPC covered list, detail, check, remove and restore of an owned fixture with actual filesystem/fingerprint checks, including persistence after packed-plugin Host restart. The background update job API, per-skill progress, batch statuses, busy rejection and cooperative cancellation are covered by local unit tests; the packed mount test keeps the same route, transaction and Client delivery path. No live public-repository or public well-known catalog coverage is claimed.

Every one of the 37 pre-final packed files was compared byte-for-byte with the frozen checkout. Real DSH revisioned Client delivery contained the packed Client bytes, which carry the background update jobs tab, progress polling and per-skill status rendering. This is not Web/Electron visual or interaction acceptance.
Ten owned CLI processes closed and every recorded POSIX group was absent before canonical owner/UID-root removal and explicit ENOENT. EPERM is uncertainty/failure, never exit evidence.

Only current DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 on the macOS isolated non-Desktop CLI/Web carrier was mounted. Desktop shell exact-Fetch dispatch is supported by the inspected SDK and real registry tests, not a live Electron acceptance check. The user's daily profile and Desktop restart remain user-owned and unverified. Other DSH versions/platforms and arbitrary escaped-daemon behavior require fresh verification.
The buffered request-body limit belongs to the DSH Connection HTTP carrier (current default 300 MiB), not this adapter or direct shared.fetch calls. No new carrier-overflow test is claimed.
